short_bio: Lindsey Vonn is a retired World Cup alpine ski racer and the most decorated American ski racer in history. Her lean high-protein diet, documented by Under Armour and MyFitnessPal, fueled her record 82 World Cup victories and sustained peak athletic performance across decades of elite competition.

base_diet.name: Lean High-Protein Athlete Diet
base_diet.description: A performance-focused omnivore eating pattern built around lean proteins, complex carbohydrates timed to training, and healthy fats. Each meal is structured to deliver dense protein and micronutrient support for muscle repair, endurance, and recovery, anchored by whole-food sources like eggs, chicken breast, salmon, quinoa, and fresh vegetables.
base_diet.philosophy: Fuel every training session with intentional macros. Eat real, whole foods at every meal, prioritize protein at each sitting to protect lean muscle, and time carbohydrates around workouts for energy and recovery. Consistency in nutrition is treated as a competitive advantage, not an afterthought.

recipes.title: Egg Scramble with Peppers, Mushrooms and Onion
recipes.description: A satisfying high-protein morning scramble built from three whole eggs sauteed with colorful bell pepper, earthy mushrooms, and yellow onion. This is the exact breakfast documented in Lindsey Vonn's performance nutrition plan and delivers approximately 22 grams of protein to start the day.

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Add diced yellow onion and diced bell pepper. Saute until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms and continue cooking until mushrooms release their moisture and begin to brown.
Pour beaten eggs over the vegetables. Season with sea salt and black pepper. Gently fold and scramble until eggs are just set.
Transfer to a plate and serve immediately.

recipes.tips: Do not overcook the eggs. Pull the pan off heat while the eggs are still slightly glossy for the best texture.

recipes.title: Roast Chicken Breast with Quinoa and Spinach
recipes.description: A powerhouse midday meal featuring a generous portion of seasoned chicken breast over fluffy quinoa and wilted spinach. Documented as Lindsey Vonn's go-to lunch, this dish delivers approximately 58 grams of protein for sustained muscle support throughout training.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 200C (400F). Season chicken breast with sea salt, black pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil.
Roast chicken breast in the oven until cooked through and internal temperature reaches 74C (165F).
Meanwhile, cook quinoa in 1 cup of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer until water is absorbed.
In a pan, heat remaining olive oil over medium heat. Add minced garlic and saute for 30 seconds, then add spinach and wilt.
Slice rested chicken and serve over quinoa alongside wilted spinach. Finish with a squeeze of lemon juice.

recipes.tips: Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes after roasting before slicing so the juices redistribute evenly.

recipes.title: Baked Salmon with Quinoa and Asparagus
recipes.description: Lindsey Vonn's documented dinner: omega-3-rich salmon fillet baked alongside tender asparagus spears, served over quinoa. This meal delivers approximately 53 grams of protein and 574 calories, supporting overnight muscle repair and recovery.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 200C (400F). Cook quinoa in 1 cup of water: bring to a boil, cover, and simmer until liquid is absorbed.
Place salmon fillet on a lined baking sheet. Toss asparagus spears in olive oil, salt, pepper, and minced garlic, and arrange alongside the salmon.
Top salmon with lemon slices. Bake until salmon flakes easily with a fork and asparagus is tender.
Serve salmon and asparagus over quinoa. Finish with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.

recipes.tips: For best texture, do not overbake the salmon. Remove from the oven as soon as it flakes with gentle pressure from a fork.

recipes.title: Almonds, Kiwi and Blueberries
recipes.description: Lindsey Vonn's documented snack: a simple trio of raw almonds, fresh kiwi, and blueberries that delivers healthy fats, antioxidants, and natural sugars for a quick energy refuel between meals or before a lighter training session.

instructions.text: Peel and slice the kiwi.
Arrange almonds, kiwi slices, and blueberries on a small plate or in a container.

recipes.tips: Measure the almonds by weight (28g is about 23 almonds) to keep the fat content consistent with the documented macros.

recipes.title: Post-Workout Egg White Omelet with Chicken, Broccoli and Bell Pepper
recipes.description: A lean, high-protein post-workout meal documented in Lindsey Vonn's performance nutrition plan. Egg whites and chicken breast deliver a rapid protein hit with minimal fat, while broccoli and bell pepper add micronutrients to support recovery.

instructions.text: Lightly coat a non-stick pan with olive oil and heat over medium heat. Add broccoli florets and diced bell pepper and saute until just tender.
Add diced cooked chicken breast to the pan and toss with vegetables to warm through.
Pour beaten egg whites over the filling. Season with sea salt and black pepper. Cook without stirring until edges are set, then fold omelet in half.
Slide onto a plate and serve immediately.

recipes.tips: Use pre-cooked chicken breast from the lunch prep batch to cut assembly time down to under 5 minutes after a workout.

recipes.title: Egg White and Spinach Scramble with Mushrooms
recipes.description: A lean, high-protein breakfast scramble built on egg whites sauteed with yellow onion, earthy mushrooms, and wilted spinach.

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Add diced yellow onion and cook until softened and translucent.
Add sliced mushrooms and cook until they release their moisture and begin to brown at the edges.
Add fresh spinach and toss with the mushroom mixture until fully wilted.
Pour beaten egg whites over the vegetables. Season with sea salt and black pepper. Gently fold and scramble until egg whites are just set and no longer translucent.
Transfer to a plate and serve immediately.

recipes.tips: Pull the pan off the heat while the egg whites still look slightly moist — carry-over heat will finish them and prevent a rubbery texture.

recipes.title: Eggs with Broccoli, Bell Pepper, and Onion
recipes.description: A whole-egg scramble loaded with broccoli florets, diced bell pepper, and yellow onion for a colorful, vegetable-forward morning plate.

instructions.text: Microwave broccoli florets with a splash of water for 90 seconds until just tender, then drain.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add diced yellow onion and bell pepper and saute until softened.
Add blanched broccoli to the pan and toss to combine with the peppers and onion.
Pour beaten eggs over the vegetables. Season with sea salt and black pepper. Fold and scramble gently until eggs are just set.
Transfer to a plate and serve immediately.

recipes.tips: Pre-blanching the broccoli prevents it from releasing excess steam in the pan, keeping the scramble from becoming watery.

recipes.title: Almond Butter Quinoa Bowl with Blueberries
recipes.description: Warm cooked quinoa stirred with almond butter until creamy, then topped with fresh blueberries and chopped almonds for a carbohydrate-forward pre-training breakfast.

instructions.text: Combine rinsed quinoa and 1 cup of water in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until all water is absorbed.
While quinoa is still hot, stir in almond butter until fully incorporated and the mixture is creamy and uniform.
Transfer to a bowl and top with fresh blueberries and chopped almonds. Drizzle with honey if desired.

recipes.tips: Stir in the almond butter immediately off the heat while the quinoa is hottest so it emulsifies smoothly into the grain.

recipes.title: Chicken Breast and Quinoa Bowl with Broccoli and Bell Pepper
recipes.description: A high-protein meal-prep bowl pairing roasted chicken breast with fluffy quinoa, steamed broccoli florets, and diced bell pepper.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 200C (400F). Rub chicken breast with olive oil, sea salt, black pepper, and garlic powder. Place on a lined baking sheet and roast until internal temperature reaches 74C (165F).
While chicken roasts, cook quinoa in 1 cup of water: bring to a boil, cover, reduce heat, and simmer until all liquid is absorbed.
Steam broccoli florets until bright green and just tender, about 4 minutes. During the last 2 minutes, add diced bell pepper to the steamer or toss it raw into the assembled bowl.
Slice the rested chicken breast and arrange over the quinoa. Add broccoli and bell pepper to the bowl and season to taste.

recipes.tips: Cook a double portion of quinoa and chicken at the start of the week to assemble this bowl in minutes on busy training days.

recipes.title: Salmon and Quinoa Bowl with Spinach and Mushrooms
recipes.description: Pan-seared salmon fillet served over quinoa with sauteed mushrooms and wilted spinach — a complete omega-3-rich midday performance bowl.

instructions.text: Cook quinoa in 1 cup of water: bring to a boil, cover, reduce heat, and simmer until all liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
Season salmon fillet with sea salt and black pepper. Heat half the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and sear salmon skin-side up for 3 minutes. Flip and cook until salmon flakes easily.
In the same skillet over medium heat, add remaining oil and saute sliced mushrooms with minced garlic until browned. Add spinach and toss until wilted.
Spoon quinoa into a bowl, top with mushrooms and spinach, then place salmon on top. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the entire bowl.

recipes.tips: Pat the salmon dry before searing to get a good crust. If the fillet has a thin tail end, fold it under to keep the thickness even during cooking.

recipes.title: Chicken, Asparagus, and Spinach Protein Bowl
recipes.description: A low-carb, high-protein lunch bowl of seasoned chicken breast with sauteed asparagus spears, sliced yellow onion, and fresh spinach.

ingredients.preparation: woody ends trimmed, cut into 5cm pieces

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add sliced yellow onion and cook until softened and lightly golden.
Add minced garlic and asparagus pieces. Saute, stirring frequently, until asparagus is bright green and just tender.
Push vegetables to one side of the pan. Add sliced chicken breast, season with sea salt and black pepper, and cook until no longer pink and cooked through.
Add fresh spinach to the pan and toss everything together until spinach wilts. Adjust seasoning and serve immediately.

recipes.tips: Slice the chicken breast thin and even so it cooks quickly in the same pan without drying out. Serve right out of the skillet to keep it warm.

recipes.title: Baked Salmon with Broccoli and Spinach
recipes.description: A simple sheet-pan dinner of herb-seasoned baked salmon fillet served alongside roasted broccoli on a bed of fresh or wilted spinach.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 200C (400F). Toss broccoli florets with half the olive oil, minced garlic, sea salt, and black pepper. Spread on one side of a lined baking sheet.
Place salmon fillet on the other side of the baking sheet. Drizzle with remaining olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and top with lemon slices.
Bake until salmon flakes easily with a fork and broccoli edges are lightly caramelized.
Arrange fresh spinach in a wide bowl or on a plate. Place hot salmon and broccoli on top so the heat gently wilts the spinach underneath.

recipes.tips: If the broccoli needs more browning, switch the oven to broil for the last 2 minutes while keeping an eye on the salmon.

recipes.title: Chicken Breast with Asparagus, Mushrooms, and Quinoa
recipes.description: A recovery dinner of roasted chicken breast alongside seared mushrooms and asparagus, served over a base of fluffy quinoa.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 200C (400F). Season chicken breast with sea salt, black pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil. Roast until internal temperature reaches 74C (165F).
While chicken roasts, cook quinoa in 1 cup of water: bring to a boil, cover, reduce heat, and simmer until all liquid is absorbed.
Heat remaining oil in a skillet over high heat. Sear mushrooms without stirring until browned on one side, then add asparagus and minced garlic. Toss and cook until asparagus is just tender.
Slice the rested chicken and arrange over quinoa. Top with mushrooms and asparagus. Finish with a squeeze of lemon juice.

recipes.tips: Resist stirring the mushrooms for the first 2 minutes so they develop a golden crust rather than steaming in their own liquid.

recipes.title: Salmon with Bell Pepper, Onion, and Broccoli
recipes.description: Pan-seared salmon fillet served alongside roasted broccoli and a quick saute of sliced bell pepper and yellow onion for a low-carb, micronutrient-rich dinner.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 200C (400F). Toss broccoli florets with a little olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast until tender and edges are lightly charred.

Season salmon with sea salt and black pepper. In an oven-safe skillet, heat oil over medium-high heat. Sear salmon skin-side down for 3 minutes, then flip and finish in the oven with the broccoli for the last 4 minutes.
While the salmon and broccoli finish, saute sliced yellow onion and bell pepper in the same skillet until softened and lightly caramelized. Add minced garlic in the last minute.
Plate the salmon alongside roasted broccoli and the pepper-onion saute. Squeeze lemon juice over everything before serving.

recipes.tips: Using an oven-safe skillet lets you start the salmon on the stovetop and finish it in the oven alongside the broccoli with minimal washing up.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter with Blueberries and Almonds
recipes.description: A no-prep snack plate of peanut butter, fresh blueberries, and raw almonds combining healthy fats, antioxidants, and quick natural energy.

instructions.text: Measure out peanut butter and place it in a small bowl or alongside a small plate.
Arrange fresh blueberries and raw almonds alongside the peanut butter. Dip the almonds or eat them separately with the blueberries.

recipes.tips: Weigh the almonds (20g is about 16 whole almonds) to keep fat and calorie counts consistent, as portion size is easy to overshoot with nuts.

recipes.title: Almond Butter and Kiwi Snack Plate
recipes.description: Sliced fresh kiwi served alongside almond butter and a small handful of whole almonds for a simple snack delivering healthy fats, antioxidants, and vitamin C.

instructions.text: Peel the kiwi and slice into rounds.
Arrange kiwi slices on a plate with almond butter in a small bowl on the side. Add raw almonds alongside for crunch.

recipes.tips: Use ripe kiwi for the best sweetness — the flesh should give slightly when pressed. Dipping each slice into the almond butter balances the tartness with fat.

recipes.title: Dark Chocolate, Almonds, and Blueberries
recipes.description: A post-training treat of antioxidant-rich dark chocolate squares paired with raw almonds and fresh blueberries for a satisfying whole-food snack.

instructions.text: Break the dark chocolate into small pieces (approximately one square) and place in the center of a small plate.
Arrange raw almonds and fresh blueberries around the chocolate. Eat together in small bites to balance the bitterness of the chocolate with the fruit and nut flavors.

recipes.tips: Choose a dark chocolate with at least 70% cacao content for the best antioxidant profile with the lowest sugar load.
